the Crossing Statistic provides an alternative method of testing the goodness of fit between data and a model that is less sensitive than χ^2 to the intrinsic errors of the data and that can be used in situations when the errors are not known.

the Crossing Statistic can provide a more complete picture of the data than χ2, and hence is a more appropriate goodness of fit statistic in situations where the dispersion of the data set is not known a priori.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new statistic for goodness of fit that can be used when the intrinsic dispersion of data is poorly understood and/or when the data are highly correlated.
the crossing statistic is a more general and powerful statistic than the χ2 statistic, and can be used as an alternative to χ2 in cases where the latter is not appropriate.
the Crossing Statistic can provide a more robust goodness of fit test than the χ2 statistic in situations where the errors are not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Crossing Statistic provides a useful alternative to χ2 when the intrinsic dispersion of data is not well known.
we can make significant progress in distinguishing between cosmological models even in the presence of poorly understood errors in the data.
there is more than one way to quantify the goodness of fit between data and models, and that different statistics can be useful for different situations.
